before.label: Decoding and sampling controls
before.definition: Parameters and rules, such as greedy, temperature, top-k, and nucleus sampling, that determine how tokens are chosen from a model's distribution.

temperature.rationale: This names a particular selection rule or parameter within the broader token-selection concept, not an equivalent name.

top-k sampling.rationale: This names a particular selection rule or parameter within the broader token-selection concept, not an equivalent name.

nucleus sampling.rationale: This names a particular selection rule or parameter within the broader token-selection concept, not an equivalent name.

top-p.rationale: This names a particular selection rule or parameter within the broader token-selection concept, not an equivalent name.

min-p.rationale: This names a particular selection rule or parameter within the broader token-selection concept, not an equivalent name.

repetition penalty.rationale: This names a particular selection rule or parameter within the broader token-selection concept, not an equivalent name.

greedy decoding.rationale: This names a particular selection rule or parameter within the broader token-selection concept, not an equivalent name.

changes.rationale: Distinguish lexical equivalence from narrower mechanisms and named implementations while retaining retrieval access.

sources.locator: GenerationConfig: decoding strategies and logits manipulation
sources.supports: The API lists temperature, top-k, top-p, min-p, repetition penalty, and greedy decoding as distinct configuration choices.

before.label: Stop conditions and output-length limits
before.definition: Rules that terminate autoregressive generation when a stopping criterion is met, including an end token, a stop sequence, or an output-token limit.

stop sequences.rationale: This names one stopping criterion or parameter, not the entire class of generation-stopping rules.

max new tokens.rationale: This names one stopping criterion or parameter, not the entire class of generation-stopping rules.

end-of-sequence handling.rationale: This names one stopping criterion or parameter, not the entire class of generation-stopping rules.

changes.rationale: Distinguish lexical equivalence from narrower mechanisms and named implementations while retaining retrieval access.

sources.supports: Output-token limits, stop strings, and end tokens are separately specified controls.

before.label: Accelerator sharing and partitioning
before.definition: Running several workloads on one accelerator by time-slicing, concurrent contexts, or hardware partitions with dedicated memory and compute slices.

MIG.rationale: NVIDIA MIG implements spatial GPU partitioning; it is not the generic sharing and partitioning concept.

SR-IOV.rationale: PCIe virtual functions can support device sharing but are not equivalent to accelerator partitioning.

GPU sharing.rationale: GPU sharing is restricted to one accelerator class within the broader accelerator-sharing concept.

changes.rationale: Distinguish lexical equivalence from narrower mechanisms and named implementations while retaining retrieval access.

sources.supports: SR-IOV exposes virtual functions on a physical PCIe device.

before.label: Model export
before.definition: Converting a framework model into an artifact with an explicit computation and input contract that a compatible runtime can execute.

TorchScript.rationale: This names a framework representation, format, or API used for export, not the general model-export process.

torch.export.rationale: This names a framework representation, format, or API used for export, not the general model-export process.

SavedModel.rationale: This names a framework representation, format, or API used for export, not the general model-export process.

changes.rationale: Distinguish lexical equivalence from narrower mechanisms and named implementations while retaining retrieval access.

sources.supports: The API produces exported program artifacts.
SavedModel is a TensorFlow program serialization format.

before.label: Modality encoder
before.definition: A network that turns images, audio, or video into token sequences for a shared backbone; visual tokens often dominate prefill cost and KV size.

vision encoder.rationale: A vision encoder handles visual input; the parent concept also covers audio and video modalities.

changes.rationale: Distinguish lexical equivalence from narrower mechanisms and named implementations while retaining retrieval access.

sources.supports: CLIP learns image representations; a vision encoder is a modality-specific component.

before.label: Generated-content watermarking
before.definition: Embedding a statistically detectable signal into generated text, images, or audio at generation time, such as by biasing token sampling, so that content can later be identified as model-generated.

output watermarking.rationale: Within this concept scope, output refers to generated content rather than marking model parameters.

text watermarking.rationale: Text is one output modality; the parent concept also includes image and audio outputs.

changes.rationale: Distinguish lexical equivalence from narrower mechanisms and named implementations while retaining retrieval access.

sources.supports: The paper describes watermarking model output by embedding detectable signals in generated text.
